title: Spot-aware reservation scheduler for capacity-safe GPU pool upgrades
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: Upgrades to dedicated GPU pools currently treat all devices as homogeneous capacity. In practice pools contain a mix of on-demand and spot preemptible devices. During waves of rolling upgrades this causes unexpected capacity cliffs when spot devices are preempted or drained in the same window as upgrades, leading to SLA violations for tenants and noisy autoscaler behavior.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, spot-aware reservation scheduler and drain rate limiter that integrates with the autoscaler contract handshake and rollout gates. The scheduler should: (1) reserve a soft capacity buffer per pool that accounts for spot volatility and tenant QoS tiers; (2) expose a deterministic upgrade schedule to the autoscaler so it can refuse evictions that would violate SLOs; (3) apply per-tenant soft-fencing so high-QoS tenants are protected from simultaneous eviction + spot loss; (4) publish observability signals and runbook links for on-call.

Scope: Dedicated fleet control plane components + autoscaler handshake + rollout gate extension + console dashboard signals and runbook. This ticket focuses on core scheduler and API contract; follow-ups will cover console UX and long-term ML-driven predictions for spot churn.

Non-goals: Rewriting the autoscaler internals; adding new pricing/commit contracts.

Success metrics: (a) no increase in 99th-token-latency error budget burn during staged rollouts vs baseline; (b) <= 1 sustained SLA violation per quarter attributable to upgrade waves; (c) autoscaler rejection rate for upgrade requests < 5% after tuning; (d) clear dashboard showing reserved vs available capacity per pool.

implementation_notes:
Core pieces: deterministic schedule generator (golang service), scheduler controller (k8s controller), autoscaler handshake endpoint (grpc + HTTP fallback), and signed schedule attestations. Backwards compat: if autoscaler doesn't support handshake, default to legacy behavior but increase drain cooldown. Metrics and tracing must be added before canary.

Testing plan: unit tests for schedule generator; integration tests with autoscaler simulator; staged canary across 3 pools (canary-1/2/3) with rollback gates tied to error budget burn and pod eviction traces.

Rollback plan: if SLOs degrade, abort in-console wave and restore previous schedule via signed rollback token. Manual failover: run emergency 'pool-freeze' which sets reserved_capacity to 100% and aborts all planned drains.
notes: Related research: reviewed spot churn stats Q4-2025 (average spot loss per pool: 18% per 24h, 95p=52%). Decided to use conservative reserve defaults: 20% for mixed pools, 10% for on-demand heavy pools. Will iterate after telemetry is collected.
